name: Dog
description: The body a player is, in the dog game: Kimi's bare Bernese mountain dog, one faceted low-poly shell of 11,457 triangles generated with the Tripo API, on Kimi's canine rig (144 bones in Blender, of which the 38 deform bones are what this file carries: hips, two spine segments, chest, neck, head, nose, jaw, two eyes, two-bone ears, a four-bone tail, fore legs of scapula, upper, lower, paw and toe, hind legs of upper, lower, hock, paw and toe), with the twelve clips a dog needs before any object speaks. The dog wears nothing: its collar, harness and packs are separate meshes skinned to the same joints and ship as their own asset. The four gaits are keyed on the rig's IK paw controls with each paw planted on the ground, so a foot in a stance does not slide; the speed each gait was authored for comes out of that geometry and is stated per clip.

sockets.name: mouth
sockets.description: Under the nose, at the tip of the jaw. The one thing movement.carry_in_mouth holds rides here, so it follows the jaw through a sniff, a bark and a drag. Parented to the jaw's deform bone.

sockets.name: collar
sockets.description: The throat, on the underside of the neck, where a collar's ring hangs and a leash clips. Parented to the neck's deform bone.

sockets.name: back
sockets.description: The top of the back behind the withers, measured off the body's surface, where a blanket or a pack is carried. Parented to the second spine segment's deform bone.

sockets.name: head_top
sockets.description: Crown of the head, between the ears, measured off the body's surface. Parented to the head's deform bone.

animations.name: idle
animations.description: A breath, a slow wag down a four-bone tail, one ear flick, a glance left and back with the eyes riding the head.

animations.name: walk
animations.description: Four-beat lateral sequence: hind left, fore left, hind right, fore right, a quarter apart. Each paw planted for a 0.36 m stance: authored for 0.774 m/s.

animations.name: trot
animations.description: Diagonal pairs half a cycle apart, paws planted for a 0.40 m stance: authored for 1.92 m/s.

animations.name: run
animations.description: Rotary gallop: the hind pair close together, then the fore pair, the back rounding and flattening under them. Paws planted for a 0.50 m stance: authored for 3.0 m/s.

animations.name: drag
animations.description: A walk with the weight back and the head low: the mouth is on something heavier than the dog lifts. Paws planted for a 0.28 m stance: authored for 0.4 m/s. movement.carry_in_mouth's dragSpeedFactor is why it is slow.

animations.name: sniff
animations.description: Nose down: the body pitches forward over planted paws, the legs fold, the neck and head drop and the nose sweeps. The mouth socket comes down to about 0.07 m.

animations.name: sniff_air
animations.description: Nose up, on the wind: the head lifts, the mouth socket to about 0.89 m, and casts slowly.

animations.name: dig
animations.description: The fore paws scrape alternately along the ground, the chest low, the rump up, the head down watching the hole, the tail up. One cycle is one scrape of each paw; housing.den_and_cache counts the seconds.

animations.name: sit
animations.description: Down onto the haunches over half a second, then held: the rump to the ground, the hocks laid down, the fore legs straight under square shoulders.

animations.name: lie
animations.description: The sphinx over a second: fore legs out in front on their elbows, hocks on the ground, the head up and then lowered. What housing.den_and_cache's rest looks like.

animations.name: bark
animations.description: Head back, jaw open 32 degrees, chest up, a hop of the fore paws; then shut. The brick drops what the mouth holds on a bark, so the open jaw is also what the player sees.

animations.name: mark
animations.description: The right hind paw lifts out and up with its hock, holds, and comes down; the weight shifts left to carry it.

source.tool: Tripo API (body, and the segmentation that split off the gear), Kimi's canine rig in Blender, and blender-mcp-asset-pipeline 1.0.3 on Blender 4.4.3 (clips, sockets, export)
source.sourceFile: Riverside Bernese Dog — Base Rig.blend, 35256608 bytes, sha256 cb33715c12010ab2e18e126af0155e93c11c9f08eec9ed03c1f9fc80bf042743, Kimi's master of 9 Nov 2026; not in either repository, named by hash in the script

provenance: The yard (game-architect-studio #150) drew its dog as nine boxes turned as one, which is an honest grey-box and cannot sit, dig or put its nose down. Four bodies followed in the studio's build script on 9 Nov 2026: the boxes rigged as they stood, a voxel-remeshed shell of them, a lofted low-poly tube body, and Kimi's first Tripo generation of the concept painting, which wore its harness and saddlebag as part of the mesh and as paint in the coat. Alexander asked for the dog with nothing on it and the gear as separate pieces, since what the dog wears changes through the game. Kimi delivered that the same day: a bare body generated with the Tripo API, the original equipment isolated into three attachment meshes by Tripo's semantic segmentation, and a 144-bone animator rig with 38 deform bones (IK/FK limbs with poles, scapulae, rear hocks, toe and heel rolls, tail follow, two-bone ears, eye aim, jaw) with normalised weights of at most four influences. Rights to Tripo output rest with the generating account under Tripo's terms, to be confirmed against the plan tier before the game is published. The studio's script appends that master by sha256 and makes the asset from it: the body welded (Tripo writes every facet with its own vertices; her weights agree on every split), flat-shaded, the coat resampled to 1K and written as JPEG, the normal and roughness maps dropped. One patch is applied to the rig and recorded as such: nothing joined the last spine segment to the chest, so pitching the hips ten degrees opened a 7.6 cm step in the back; that segment now aims at and stretches to the chest, and the build checks the step is gone. The master carries an idle and a walk; its walk covers 0.15 m/s and a game needs gaits at known speeds, so the twelve clips here are keyed by the script on her controls and sampled onto the deform bones by the exporter. Her IK does not stretch, so each paw is pivoted heel-up about its toes by just enough to stay within reach of the shoulder or hip as the body stands on that frame, the body stands 12 mm below her rest pose because her forelegs rest 99.4% straight, and the build measures every leg joint in every clip and fails if one opens more than 5 mm. Clips are named for a pack's bricks: sniff and sniff_air for world.scent_field's two nose modes, drag for movement.carry_in_mouth's heavy things, dig and lie for housing.den_and_cache, bark and mark for the two inputs that lay or drop scent. The rig lessons come from P2Design's course squirrel, used as a reference and never as an asset.
